paper.title: A Real-World WebAgent with Planning, Long Context Understanding, and Program Synthesis
paper.central_claim: WebAgent (HTML-T5 planning + HTML summarisation with self-experience supervision, Flan-U-PaLM grounded program synthesis) improves real-website success by over 50% (~70-80%); HTML-T5 gives +18.7% on MiniWoB++ and SoTA on Mind2Web (authors' original claim).

aggregate_session_reason: CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID inherited from the controller session; both seat records carry the same id, so it does not distinguish seats. No receipt; no model probe.

evidence.quote: Our proposed WebAgent achieves around 70-80% success on real websites via self-experience supervision, outperforming single LLM approach by over 50%
evidence.support_explanation: Author headline system claim (preserved as original central claim).

evidence.quote: The raw HTML content of the newly opened page is extracted and fed into HTML-T5 along with the user’s instruction and previous planning steps.
evidence.support_explanation: Closed-loop observation: each new page's raw HTML plus instruction and history re-enter HTML-T5.

evidence.quote: This iterative process of planning, summarization, and program synthesis continues until a designated end-of-episode sub-instruction is predicted or the maximum number of iterations is reached.
evidence.support_explanation: Stop rule: end-of-episode sub-instruction or an iteration cap whose value is never given.

evidence.quote: Subsequently, it generates the next sub-instruction (e.g. type in 7500 into max rent ) and extracts the relevant data-ref attributes used for retrieving HTML snippets.
evidence.support_explanation: HTML-T5 output interface: next sub-instruction + data-ref references used to cut snippets.

evidence.quote: Provided with few-shot generic examples (such as selecting checkboxes, entering text into inputs, clicking on options, and scrolling etc.) for program generation
evidence.support_explanation: Programmer prompt content described only generically; the few-shot prompt itself is not given.

evidence.quote: We employ a rule-based parser to decompose instructions into sequences of sub-instructions; corresponding reference IDs are retrieved from HTML using regular expressions.
evidence.support_explanation: Self-experience labels come from hand-written scripts (plan) and regex retrieval (snippets).

evidence.quote: The success of recorded demonstrations varies, and automating success criteria for real-world tasks remains challenging.
evidence.support_explanation: Authors concede demonstrations are not success-verified.

evidence.quote: we utilize environmental feedback to eliminate critical failures, such as program execution errors, retriever errors, and clearly erroneous URL prefixes
evidence.support_explanation: Only quality gate: post-hoc removal of execution/retriever/URL failures; precision of the filter not audited.

evidence.quote: We maintain a collection of instruction templates that incorporate placeholders such as “Show me the way from <start> to <goal> by <n-th> <transportation> at map website
evidence.support_explanation: Training instructions are template instantiations (map template quoted).

evidence.quote: 1. Show me the way from San Jose to Mountain View by 2nd Cycling at map website.
evidence.support_explanation: First map TEST instruction is a direct instance of the same training template; slot-value overlap with training not reported.

evidence.quote: we curate 260 episodes on real estate website, 230 episodes on social media website, and 410 episodes on map website to finetune HTML-T5.
evidence.support_explanation: Self-experience data are collected on the very three sites used for evaluation.

evidence.quote: We prepare 20 different natural language instructions
evidence.support_explanation: Live denominator: 20 instructions per site (60 total), single run.

evidence.quote: If the agents achieve 100 score, that episode will mark as success.
evidence.support_explanation: Success = full attribute coverage; who grades coverage and how is not specified.

evidence.quote: we have carefully conducted the experiments under human supervision in case undesired behaviors happen.
evidence.support_explanation: Live runs are human-supervised; intervention policy/grading protocol not reported.

evidence.quote: We have anonymized the real websites we tested on for safety and privacy concerns.
evidence.support_explanation: Sites anonymized: no external replication of the live result possible.
Table 1 WebAgent row: 65/70/80% success; error ratios by type (re/sm/map).
Table 1 single-generalist baseline: 10/20/10% success.
Planner-only module ablation (fixed programmer): 50/20/30%.

evidence.quote: Without language model modules, prompted Flan-U-PaLM plans in an open-loop manner ( Plan : ✗ ) and regular-expression-based retrieval summarizes HTML inputs
evidence.support_explanation: Baselines' removed modules are replaced by open-loop prompting / regex: finetuning, closed-loop and data co-vary.

evidence.quote: task planning should be learned by finetuning domain language models for closed-loop planning, rather than by prompting single LLM for open-loop planning.
evidence.support_explanation: Authors attribute gain to self-experience finetuning + closed loop, which Table 1 does not separate.

evidence.quote: in real-estate , WebAgent generates incorrect plans in 70% of failure episodes
evidence.support_explanation: Planning is the dominant residual failure.

evidence.quote: real-estate requires long-horizon planning (about 20 steps per episode)
evidence.support_explanation: Only approximate per-site horizons; no step cap / steps-used per method.

evidence.quote: Such a large model, however, makes it challenging to reflect the feedback about the errors in generated code, compared to smaller models.
evidence.support_explanation: No program-error feedback or repair in the loop.

evidence.quote: which, however, might cause additional computational costs and latency.
evidence.support_explanation: Cost/latency only acknowledged qualitatively.

evidence.quote: As we demonstrated in Mind2Web, our method could generalize across the internet if we have enough data.
evidence.support_explanation: Author generalisation claim rests on offline Mind2Web.

evidence.quote: This highlights that HTML-T5 can handle real-world web automation tasks better and shows generalization beyond our real-world evaluation with 3 websites.
evidence.support_explanation: Offline step metrics promoted to a 'beyond our real-world evaluation' generalisation statement.
Mind2Web HTML-T5-XL: cross-task/website/domain step SR 57.8/42.9/48.3 (offline, held-out splits).

evidence.quote: We leverage the cached candidate generation results and direct QA formulation by following
evidence.support_explanation: Mind2Web protocol inherited from Deng et al. (cached candidates).

evidence.quote: HTML-T5-XL (ours) | 67.1 % | +6.7
evidence.support_explanation: Table 3: HTML-T5-XL 12K = 67.1% (basis of +18.7 over WebN-T5-XL 48.4).
Appendix J per-task average for HTML-T5-XL 12K = 0.655, inconsistent with Table 3's 67.1%.

evidence.quote: We here evaluate HTML-T5 on 56 simulated tasks in MiniWoB++ using 100 evaluation episodes per task.
evidence.support_explanation: MiniWoB++: executable simulator reward, 100 episodes/task.

evidence.quote: preparing 130 demonstrations and splitting them into train (90%) and test splits (10%).
evidence.support_explanation: Offline real-estate planning test split is ~13 demonstrations from the live-evaluation site.

evidence.quote: We report the best per-step exact match accuracy in test set.
evidence.support_explanation: Best value selected on the test split; the same metric chooses the span mixture (Table 2 right).

evidence.quote: HTML-denoising generally improves the performance on offline task planning on real estate website and MiniWoB
evidence.support_explanation: Span-length choice judged on real-estate offline planning + MiniWoB.

evidence.quote: Local and global attention matches to the hierarchical tree structure of HTML, and then improves the success rate by over 18%
evidence.support_explanation: Same-data architecture ablation (component causality).

evidence.quote: HTML-denoising also yields better the success rate than instruction tuned ones.
evidence.support_explanation: Same-data objective comparison vs Flan-LongT5 across sizes.

evidence.quote: 9 imply that the performance of Flan-U-PaLM-540B and gpt-3.5-turbo are the same (80% success, 93.8% score)
evidence.support_explanation: Programmer swap with planner fixed (map only).

evidence.quote: In addition, Flan-PaLM-8B could not generate proper programs at all.
evidence.support_explanation: Programmer-capacity boundary.

evidence.quote: Compared to simulator (about 0.5K tokens on average), HTML tokens of real websites are much longer (from 7K to 14K), which takes up the context length of large language models.
evidence.support_explanation: Gap evidence: real-site HTML length vs simulators.

evidence.quote: While MindAct also combines several language models, it has just adopted DeBERTa
evidence.support_explanation: Authors' positioning vs nearest neighbour MindAct.

evidence.quote: In contrast, longer spans can contain more semantically meaningful chunks
evidence.support_explanation: Targeted property of the long-span objective (asserted, not probed).

evidence.quote: use dev set for the evaluation
evidence.support_explanation: WebSRC evaluated on dev set.

evidence.quote: For GPT-4 we use 50 50 tasks for each setting with top- 10 10 candidates due to limited budget.
evidence.support_explanation: Mind2Web's GPT-4 MindAct baseline is a 50-task-per-split, top-10-candidate subset; WebAgent Table 4 compares to it without marking the subset.

signatures.object: Modular live-web policy (static design, trained specialist)
signatures.information: Instruction, raw HTML of current page, previous sub-instructions and previous snippet IDs (DOM privilege, no screenshots).
signatures.operation: HTML-T5 predicts next sub-instruction + data-ref -> snippet extraction -> few-shot Flan-U-PaLM writes Selenium code -> execute -> next HTML.
signatures.conditions: Parseable DOM, same-site self-experience data, >=62B-class code model.
signatures.feedback: Next-page HTML only; no program-error or goal verification.
signatures.selection_rule: End-of-episode sub-instruction or unstated iteration cap.
signatures.data: Template instructions, scripted plans, regex refs, generated programs filtered on execution/retriever/URL errors; 260/230/410 episodes.
signatures.failure_boundary: Planning dominant; no held-out live site; cost unmeasured.

gap.author_gap: Real sites: open-ended action space, long messy HTML, LLMs lacking HTML inductive bias.
gap.checked_gap: Length gap quantified; MindAct already filters HTML with a small LM and predicts actions offline; ReAct-style closed loops pre-exist. Residue: learned joint plan+snippet prediction feeding executable programs on live sites.
gap.residue: Live executable action generation from long HTML with learned planning/extraction.
gap.stakes: Plan/snippet errors compound over page transitions.
gap.method_response: HTML-T5 specialist + self-experience finetuning + program synthesis.
gap.remaining_gap: Planning errors, no verification/repair, no held-out live transfer, unmeasured cost.
unresolved: ReAct/WebShop lineage taken from sol's reading of shared references; not re-read by the aggregator (no score dependence).

matches.operation: Replace a categorical action space by generated Selenium programs conditioned on sub-instruction + snippet.

Interface matched to available DOM; no bounded tool library.

matches.reason: Action-interface redesign (act via programming); no visual grounder.

rejected.reason: C10 = generalist planner describes target, specialist grounder localises it; here the specialist both plans and localises (data-ref), the generalist only writes selector code, and nothing is visual.
C11 = mix GUI actions with code/shell/SDK; WebAgent acts by code only, no GUI primitives mixed or compared (S6).

unassigned: Instruction-first template/script synthesis has no exact GUI sub-card (exploration_driven_task_synthesis is exploration-first).

revision_proposals.text: Template+script+LLM-program+error-filter synthesis is an instruction-first baseline usable as S1 contrast; single paper, pending a second independent full text (carried from son55, unchecked).

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: Specialist reduces long HTML to snippet artifacts handed to the programmer.
pattern_mapping.necessary_conditions: Parseable DOM with stable references; adequate extraction recall.
pattern_mapping.differences: Learned, plan-coupled extraction; no rule-based restructuring or token accounting.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: Sub-instruction+snippet -> generated Selenium program changes the model-computer action interface.
pattern_mapping.necessary_conditions: DOM locators; strong code model (>=62B or gpt-3.5 class on map).
pattern_mapping.differences: No visual grounder, no verified repair, no hybrid action space.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: Scripted/generated same-site demonstrations, coarse failure filter, specialist fine-tuning.
pattern_mapping.necessary_conditions: Script coverage of target sites; meaningful filter.
pattern_mapping.differences: Instruction-first, single round; no GUI sub-card.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: HTML long-span denoising pretraining of the specialist.
pattern_mapping.necessary_conditions: HTML corpus where long spans carry structural tokens.
pattern_mapping.differences: Not a GUI-loop operation; no domain card.

claims.text: WebAgent reaches 65/70/80% success on three real websites, >50 pp over a single Flan-U-PaLM.
claims.setting: Anonymized real-estate / social-media / map sites, DOM input, human-supervised, HTML-T5 (finetuned on 260/230/410 same-site episodes) + Flan-U-PaLM 540B.
claims.baseline_control: Single prompted Flan-U-PaLM (open-loop plan, regex snippets); +P; +S; same programmer. No equal-data or finetuned single-model control.
claims.selection_vs_test: Training episodes and 20 test instructions/site from the same sites and templates; disjointness unreported.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Author-reported large same-site live gain of the full modular system over prompted single-LLM baselines; not attributable to self-experience vs closed loop vs module presence, not transfer.

claims.text: HTML-T5-XL beats WebN-T5-XL by 18.7% on MiniWoB++ (12K).
claims.allowed_conclusion: ~17-19 pt gain (internal inconsistency); HTML-denoising adds +3 to +7 over LongT5 at equal data.

claims.text: HTML-T5 is SoTA on Mind2Web, surpassing MindAct (Flan-T5-XL, GPT-4) and Synapse.
claims.baseline_control: MindAct Flan-T5-XL same data; GPT-4 on 50-task subset.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Supported vs same-data MindAct Flan-T5-XL offline; GPT-4 comparison not like-for-like.

claims.text: The method could generalise across the internet / beyond the 3 websites.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Unsupported for the system; offline component generalisation only.

assessment.evidence_level_reason: Live-site execution (human-graded attribute coverage) and MiniWoB++ executable reward; live sites are the self-experience construction sites, so not transfer (EVIDENCE rule 2); Mind2Web is offline.
assessment.original_claim_preserved: modular recipe improves the success on real websites by over 50%; HTML-T5 +18.7% on MiniWoB++, SoTA on Mind2Web, could generalise across the internet.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: On 60 template-style instructions over three anonymized live sites that also supplied its finetuning episodes, the full WebAgent (finetuned HTML-T5 planner/extractor + Flan-U-PaLM programmer) completes 65/70/80% vs 10/20/10% for a prompted single LLM (single human-supervised run, author-reported). HTML-denoising improves over same-data LongT5 on MiniWoB++, and HTML-T5-XL beats same-data MindAct offline on Mind2Web.

G.reason: Concrete real-web bottlenecks (open action space, 7-14K-token HTML vs 0.5K in simulators, no HTML inductive bias) with nearest neighbour MindAct pinned and the residue stated (offline MCQ vs live executable programs). Not 4: decomposition / snippet filtering / closed loop are prior (MindAct, ReAct); lineage beyond MindAct only via citations. Both seats 3; endorsed.

M.reason: Each module answers a named bottleneck (long HTML -> learned snippet extraction; open actions -> program synthesis; long horizon -> closed-loop sub-instruction prediction; HTML bias -> local/global attention + long-span denoising) and yields testable predictions (planning-dominant failures, attention/objective ablations). Not 4: self-experience vs module vs closed-loop contributions not separable by design; long-span 'property' asserted. Both seats 3; endorsed.

X.reason: Loop reconstructible from text + Figure 6: inputs (instruction, raw HTML, previous sub-instructions AND previous snippet IDs) -> sub-instruction + data-ref -> snippet -> few-shot Flan-U-PaLM Selenium program -> execute -> new HTML; training trace (templates, rule parser, regex refs, generated programs, execution/retriever/URL filter, 260/230/410 same-site episodes, fine-tune). Failure boundaries partly explicit (planning-dominant errors, programmer capacity 8B/62B/540B). Not 4: iteration cap value, filter precision, actual few-shot prompt absent; Figure 6 program selects via an undocumented is-snippet attribute and Figures 5/8 elide selectors; no error recovery/rollback; transfer boundary untested. Not 2: interface and information visibility are no longer unclear once Figure 6 is read (son55's 2 was formed without the figures).

E.measurement.reason: Live outcome = 100% attribute coverage under human supervision; grader identity, intervention rule, inter-rater checks unreported; sites anonymized. MiniWoB++ has executable reward; Mind2Web offline gold. GPT-4 Mind2Web baseline is a 50-task subset, unmarked in Table 4; Table 3 (67.1) vs Appendix J (65.5) inconsistency for HTML-T5-XL 12K. Both seats 2; endorsed.

E.causality.reason: Fixed-programmer module ablations (Table 1), same-data attention/objective/initialisation ablations and a programmer swap are real controls. But baselines replace modules with open-loop prompting/regex, so finetuning on 260-410 same-site episodes, closed-loop planning and module presence co-vary; no HTML-T5-without-self-experience or equal-data single-model control; 'surpassing GPT-4' rests on a subset. Both seats 2; endorsed.

E.holdout.reason: Headline live result is on the same three sites whose self-experience episodes trained HTML-T5, with test instructions instantiated from the same templates (map #1 = template example) and no reported slot/instruction disjointness; the offline real-estate planning metric reports the best test-split value and that metric picked the span mixture. Held-out evidence exists only for the component offline (Mind2Web cross-website/domain) and is then promoted to an 'across the internet' claim. Some relevant held-out evidence (so not 0) but the central claim's holdout is essentially absent (so not 2).

E.statistics.reason: 60 live episodes, single run, success in 5-pt steps (n=20/site), no CI or repeats; real-estate error ratios (20/70/10% of 7 failures) do not reconcile with integer counts; MiniWoB 100 episodes/task single training run. Some granularity (per-site, per-task tables, error types). Both seats 1; endorsed.
